issues.failure_explanation: Two independent failures. (1) Ill-definedness: the boundary pairings (Δu, ∇v·ν), (Δu, v) and (n^T(Hu)n, ·) on ∂Ω require traces of Δu and of n^T(Hu)n, which do not exist for u ∈ H²(Ω): {Δu : u ∈ H²∩H¹₀} = L²(Ω), and L² functions have no boundary trace. (2) Wrong formulation: with F = α∂_νΔu + β∂_νw − ∂_νu and M = αΔu + βw (w = n^T(Hu)n), Green's identity gives ∫PDE·v = [volume] + (F,v)_∂Ω − (M,∂_νv)_∂Ω; the printed eq:BFHard (whose β-term also has the wrong sign: the derivation and eq:BFImpedance give −β(w,∂_νv)) equals ∫PDE·v − (F,v)_∂Ω, so the weak problem on X = H² encodes only the single condition F = 0, not the two stated sound-hard BCs; similarly eq:BFImpedance encodes only F = iθ(M − u). A 4th-order problem with one boundary condition has an infinite-dimensional kernel, so these variational problems do not represent eq:HKBC and cannot be well-posed. Moreover, the stated impedance BC (∂_nΔu − iθ(Δu + (β/α)w − (β/α)∂_nw)) is inconsistent with eq:BFImpedance, which corresponds to α∂_νΔu + β∂_νw = iθ(αΔu + βw).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reformulate both problems with essential boundary conditions (for sound hard: X = {u ∈ H² : ∂_νu = 0} with the volume-only form, which is well defined); for impedance no H²-based weak formulation of these boundary conditions is available in the source, since the needed traces exceed H², so a different formulation or regularity framework is required.
issues.overall_effect: The continuous well-posedness analysis for sound-hard and impedance boundary conditions (two of the three advertised boundary types) is unsupported: the operators 𝒜 and K, their compactness and injectivity lemmas, and the abstract existence/uniqueness claims for these cases rest on forms that are not defined on X × X and do not encode the stated boundary value problems.
issues.title: Sound-hard and impedance weak forms are ill-defined and underdetermined on X = H^2(Omega)
issues.why_classification: Two of the three advertised boundary-condition regimes have no valid variational formulation, and the impedance case admits no source-supported repair within H², so a central part of the promised well-posedness theory must be rebuilt or abandoned.

issues.why_classification: The advertised Nitsche discretization for the nematic sound-soft problem fails as analyzed, but a comparable result survives via the strongly-imposed variant available within the source's own framework.
